page: Amazon Web Services r8gd.4xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by an AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor. Operating on the arm64 architecture, this instance features 16 dedicated physical cores running at 2.8 GHz with one thread per core. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of memory, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes 950 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage. The system runs on the Nitro hypervisor and provides an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark results indicate strong memory subsystem performance, with the Passmark memory score placing in the top tier (top 10%). Large-block uncached memory read and write bandwidth tests both rank in the top 25%. Computational performance is solid, with multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Geekbench multi-core scores also reaching the top 25%. However, single-core stress-ng and Geekbench scores remain in the middle 50%. Large language model inference performance is mixed, with text generation on a medium 7B model scoring in the middle 50%, while text generation on a large 70B model falls into the bottom 10%.

From a resource density perspective, this instance offers high memory capacity and integrated local NVMe storage, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads requiring high memory-to-vCPU ratios without the overhead of separate network-attached storage. The combination of top-tier memory performance and strong database benchmark results makes this server well-suited for database operations, memory-intensive caching layers, and data decompression tasks. It is less suited for large-scale LLM inference due to the lack of hardware acceleration and lower performance on larger models.
